answer_sentence: As of {month}, a 1 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond lists at a Market Median of £275 inc-VAT across two UK retailers (Quality Diamonds fell below the publication minimum this edition, at every weight); 1.5 carat is £371 (down 4% from August) and 2 carat £487 (up 5%, also now on two retailers).
quotable_facts: In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 1 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £275 including VAT, across two retailers (Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds); Quality Diamonds fell below the 30-listing publication minimum this edition.

In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 1.5 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £371 including VAT, down 4% from £387 in August 2026, on Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds (Quality Diamonds below the minimum).

In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 2 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £487 including VAT, up 5% from £466 in August 2026, now also on two retailers (Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds) rather than three.

Quality Diamonds' UK lab-grown inventory contracted 82% between August and September 2026 (402 to 74 listings collected), and after a same-day correction to the site's Excellent-cut filter, all three of its cells fell below the 30-listing publication minimum this edition.

The September 2026 edition of the Rings.com UK Lab-Grown Diamond Price Index collected 2,213 round G VS1 IGI listings from three UK online retailers on September 17, 2026, across the three carat bands (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter is applied).
citation_line: Cite as: Rings.com UK Lab-Grown Diamond Price Index, {month} edition, rings.com/pages/uk-lab-grown-diamond-price-index.
data_notes: Sources: three retailers scraped September 17, 2026, totaling 2,213 round G VS1 IGI listings collected across the three carat bands (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter; published cells are narrower, see each retailer's note). Quality Diamonds' listed inventory contracted sharply: 74 listings collected across the three cells this edition (16 at 1ct, 28 at 1.5ct, 30 at 2ct) against 402 in August (77, 147, 178). A live re-query on 2026-09-17 (the same day as the collection) confirmed the current count (16, 29, 30) matches the September 17 collection closely, so this is a genuine inventory contraction at the retailer, not a collection issue. Same-day correction (2026-09-18): Quality Diamonds' cut filter never actually restricted its raw collection to Excellent-cut (the API's SelectedCutVals parameter does not do what it was assumed to do); fixed in the scraper and reapplied to this edition's already-captured data. Filtered to Excellent-only, Quality Diamonds' three cells fall to n=6, n=11, n=9, all below the 30-listing minimum, so none are published this edition. Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both cleared the minimum at every weight (unaffected by this fix; Diamond Labs already applied the same filter, 77 Diamonds' API returns Excellent-only server-side). Market Median: all three weights now draw on two retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds) instead of three.

retailers.note: Listed inventory fell 82% this edition (402 to 74 listings across the three cells); a live re-query the following day confirmed the drop is genuine, not a collection issue. Same-day correction (2026-09-18): the scraper's cut filter never actually restricted to Excellent-cut (raw collection mixes Excellent and Ideal); fixed and reapplied to this edition's already-captured data, which drops all three cells below the 30-listing minimum. See Coverage this edition.

1ct.note: Below the 30-listing minimum on the corrected Excellent-only count (was n=77 in August, also thin once Excellent-filtered: n=17). See Coverage this edition.

1.5ct.note: Below the 30-listing minimum on the corrected Excellent-only count (was n=147 in August, n=84 Excellent-filtered, still published then). See Coverage this edition.

2ct.note: Below the 30-listing minimum on the corrected Excellent-only count (was n=178 in August, n=71 Excellent-filtered, still published then; this edition's inventory collapse combined with the filter fix pushes it below the minimum for the first time). See Coverage this edition.

key_findings: Quality Diamonds is unpublished at all three weights this edition, after a same-day fix to a methodology gap that had been silently affecting every prior edition. Its listed inventory collapsed 82% (402 to 74 listings collected, confirmed genuine via a live re-check of the retailer's own API). Separately, and more consequentially: Quality Diamonds' raw collection has always mixed Excellent and Ideal cut stones, and unlike Diamond Labs (which already filters to Excellent-only client-side), Quality Diamonds never applied that filter, despite this index's stated Excellent-cut benchmark. Fixed today and reapplied to this edition's data: filtered to Excellent-only, all three cells fall to single digits (n=6, 11, 9), below the 30-listing minimum. The same filter, applied to August's archived data, would have left 1.5ct and 2ct essentially unchanged (comfortably above the minimum, prices within £1/ct) but would have made August's published 1ct figure thin too (n=17). August's published numbers are not being restated: every edition is a frozen snapshot once published, so this fix applies from this edition forward only. See Coverage this edition.

All three Market Medians now draw on two retailers instead of three, and the 2ct figure moved as a result. 1ct: £275 (Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds), down 2% from August's three-retailer £281. 1.5ct: £371, down 4% from £387. 2ct: £487, up 5% from August's three-retailer £466 — with Quality Diamonds now excluded, this is a genuinely different, smaller retailer set than August's, not a clean like-for-like comparison at any of the three weights this edition.

Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both raised prices at every weight. Per carat, ex-VAT, August to September: Diamond Labs +2% at 1ct (£202 to £207), +2% at 1.5ct (£168 to £172), +9% at 2ct (£158 to £172); 77 Diamonds +7% at 1ct (£234 to £251), +5% at 1.5ct (£229 to £241), +2% at 2ct (£230 to £234). Every published cell at both retailers moved in the same direction this edition.

At every weight, the published price gap now reflects just two retailers, not three. At 1ct, Diamond Labs (£207) against 77 Diamonds (£251) is a £44 gap per carat, ex-VAT, on the same benchmark specification; in August the same two retailers were £32 apart (£202 to £234), while Quality Diamonds, no longer published at this weight, was the priciest at £268. At 2ct, the spread between the two now-published retailers is £62: Diamond Labs £172 (cheapest) to 77 Diamonds £234 (priciest); Quality Diamonds no longer has a published 2ct figure to compare (its own collected count, £197, is no longer shown as a qualifying market figure, see Coverage this edition).

What UK buyers assume is a cross-border premium is VAT and exchange rate, not markup. Brilliant Earth UK is excluded from this index: their GBP prices are derived from a USD conversion formula, not independently set for the UK market.

Three of six audited UK retailers qualified at launch, and the panel is unchanged. London-based Queensmith passed structural eligibility but carries zero G-color lab-grown diamonds. Their inventory is exclusively D, E, and F color, confirmed via live API across all carat bands at launch. A three-retailer panel at G VS1 is not a methodology gap. It is the market.
All prices inc-VAT (20% UK VAT included). Ex-VAT figures are in the methodology section.
The UK index tracks G VS1, the highest-volume lab-grown specification across UK retailers. The Rings.com US index uses E VS1. Not directly comparable. E commands a color premium over G.

methodology.title: Scope
methodology.body: This index tracks listed retail prices (not transaction prices) across major UK online lab-grown diamond retailers. The September 2026 edition collected 2,213 round G VS1 IGI lab-grown diamond listings (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter) across three retailers. All prices are in GBP, inclusive of 20% UK VAT (inc-VAT). Data was collected on September 17, 2026. This is the fifth edition; the retailer panel is unchanged since the May 2026 inaugural edition.

methodology.title: Coverage this edition
methodology.body: Quality Diamonds' listed inventory contracted sharply between the August and September collections: 74 listings collected this edition (16 at 1ct, 28 at 1.5ct, 30 at 2ct) against 402 in August (77, 147, 178). A live re-query of the retailer's own inventory API on 2026-09-17 (the same day as the collection) returned near-identical counts (16, 29, 30), confirming the drop is a genuine change in listed stock rather than a collection issue. Same-day correction (2026-09-18): Quality Diamonds' cut filter has never actually restricted its raw collection to Excellent-cut, despite this index's stated Excellent-cut benchmark — the retailer's API parameter that was assumed to do this (SelectedCutVals) does not, and the raw collection mixes Excellent and Ideal cut stones (this edition: 26 Excellent, 48 Ideal, of 74). Diamond Labs' scraper already filters client-side for the identical reason (its own API mixes Excellent and Ideal too); Quality Diamonds never had that same filter. Fixed in the scraper and reapplied to this edition's already-captured data: filtered to Excellent-only, Quality Diamonds' three cells fall to n=6, n=11, n=9, below the 30-listing minimum at every weight, so none are published this edition. Checked against August's archived data for scale: the same filter would have left August's 1.5ct (n=147 to n=84) and 2ct (n=178 to n=71) cells comfortably published with prices within £1/ct of what was actually published, but would have made August's published 1ct figure (n=77 to n=17) thin. August's published figures are not being restated — every edition is a frozen snapshot once published — so this fix applies from this edition forward only. Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both cleared the minimum at every weight, unaffected by this fix; both collections were made September 17, 2026, with no feed issues.

methodology.title: Month-over-month
methodology.body: Per carat, ex-VAT, August to September: Diamond Labs +2% at 1ct (£202 to £207), +2% at 1.5ct (£168 to £172), +9% at 2ct (£158 to £172); 77 Diamonds +7% at 1ct (£234 to £251), +5% at 1.5ct (£229 to £241), +2% at 2ct (£230 to £234); Quality Diamonds not comparable at any weight this edition (all three cells fell below the publication minimum once correctly filtered to Excellent-cut, see Coverage this edition). Published Market Medians: 1ct £275, down 2% from August's three-retailer £281, now on two retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds); 1.5ct £371, down 4% from £387, also now on two retailers; 2ct £487, up 5% from August's three-retailer £466, also now on two retailers. None of the three month-over-month Market Median moves this edition are a clean like-for-like comparison: all three now draw on a different, smaller retailer set than August's.

methodology.title: Retailer panel
methodology.body: This edition tracks three retailers: Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds, and Quality Diamonds. The panel was established in May 2026, when eight retailers were evaluated and three qualified, and it is unchanged for August 2026. Two retailers (Brilliant Earth UK and James Allen) were screened out before formal audit: both price in GBP via USD conversion rather than independently setting UK prices. Six retailers proceeded to formal audit against four criteria: (1) live filterable inventory API with no credentials required, (2) publicly visible per-listing GBP pricing, (3) IGI certification as a filterable and per-listing attribute, and (4) minimum 30 qualifying listings per carat cell. Three qualified. Three were excluded; exclusion reasons are documented in the Excluded retailers note below. The panel is fixed and disclosed for comparability. Any additions, removals, or reclassifications will be explicitly noted in that month's report.

methodology.title: Excluded retailers
methodology.body: Queensmith (queensmith.co.uk) passed structural eligibility criteria but stocks exclusively D, E, and F color lab-grown diamonds: a live API query found zero G-color listings across all three benchmark carat bands, consistent with their premium-positioning sourcing standard. Purely Diamonds (purelydiamonds.co.uk) and Angelic Diamonds (angelicdiamonds.com) are finished jewelry retailers with no loose diamond search inventory.

methodology.title: Price inputs
methodology.body: Prices are the publicly visible list price at the time of data collection. Published figures in the index table include 20% UK VAT applied to the collected ex-VAT price. Ex-VAT medians (per carat) for September 2026: Diamond Labs 1ct £207 (n=64), 1.5ct £172 (n=273), 2ct £172 (n=45). 77 Diamonds 1ct £251 (n=229), 1.5ct £241 (n=775), 2ct £234 (n=265). Quality Diamonds below the publication minimum at every weight this edition once correctly filtered to Excellent-cut (n=6, n=11, n=9; see Coverage this edition). The following are excluded: promotional codes, membership discounts, negotiated pricing, and strikethrough compare-at or was-£X reference prices.

methodology.title: Benchmark specification
methodology.body: The benchmark specification is G color, VS1 clarity, round brilliant, Excellent cut, IGI-certified. G color was chosen because it is the highest-volume specification available with consistent depth across the tracked UK retailers. Three weight cells are tracked: 1ct (0.95-1.05ct), 1.5ct (1.45-1.55ct), and 2ct (1.95-2.05ct). Note: the Rings.com US price index uses E color rather than G color. E is a higher color grade and commands a price premium. Cross-market comparisons between the US and UK indices should account for this grade difference.

methodology.title: Statistical method
methodology.body: Each published figure is the median total stone price across all qualifying listings within that cell. Median is used instead of an average to reduce the influence of extreme outlier listings. A minimum of 30 qualifying listings per retailer is required for that retailer's cell to be published, and a Market Median requires at least two qualifying retailers in that cell; a single retailer's price is shown individually but is not published as a market figure. Per-cell sample sizes (n) are visible as tooltips when hovering over any price in the table. Quality Diamonds fell below the retailer threshold at every weight this edition once correctly filtered to Excellent-cut (n=6, n=11, n=9; see Coverage this edition); Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds met the threshold at every weight.

methodology.title: Deduplication
methodology.body: Listings are deduplicated within each retailer by URL. Stones with identical IGI certificate numbers may appear at more than one retailer and are counted as independent listings at each retailer where they appear.

methodology.title: Data sourcing
methodology.body: The UK index is built from live API queries against each retailer's product inventory backend. All three APIs are public-facing endpoints that power the retailers' own consumer-facing search pages. No credentials, scraper accounts, or private API keys were used.

methodology.title: Market concentration
methodology.body: The UK online lab-grown market is tracked here across three retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds, and Quality Diamonds): the primary UK-accessible online retailers with independently-priced GBP inventory and sufficient benchmark-matching stock to produce stable medians across all three carat tiers. A pricing decision by a single UK retailer will move the index median more than an equivalent decision would move the US index.

methodology.title: Comparability
methodology.body: The UK and US indices are not directly comparable: the UK index uses G VS1 and reports in GBP inc-VAT; the US index uses E VS1 and reports in USD. Historical index figures may not be directly comparable when the benchmark specification, the retailer panel, or the set of retailers with published cells changes; this edition's Market Medians all draw on two retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds) instead of three, after Quality Diamonds' listed inventory fell below the publication minimum at every weight (both a genuine inventory contraction and a same-day fix to the site's Excellent-cut filter; see Coverage this edition).

methodology.title: Independence
methodology.body: Rings.com receives no compensation from the retailers included in this index for inclusion or ranking, and no retailer has any editorial control over the methodology or results. This index reflects public list prices only; individual purchase prices may differ due to custom configurations, time-sensitive promotions, or VAT treatment at purchase.

jsonld_description: Monthly benchmark prices for lab-grown diamonds (G VS1 Round Excellent IGI-certified) across major UK online retailers. September 2026 edition collected 2,213 round G VS1 IGI listings across three retailers (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter): Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds, and Quality Diamonds. All prices in GBP, inclusive of 20% UK VAT. All three cells carry a two-retailer Market Median this edition (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds) after Quality Diamonds fell below the publication minimum at every weight.
